newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound Palestinian during Hebron protest.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound Palestinian during Hebron protest.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded a Palestinian on Tuesday in a further flareup of violence in Hebron over posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig, witnesses said.

Dozens of Arab youths broke away from a peaceful demonstration which Palestinian dignitaries called in response to the discovery of the crudely drawn posters and hurled rocks at soldiers and Jewish settlers in the divided West Bank town.
Soldiers responded by firing rubber-coated metal bullets, wounding one youngster, the witnesses said.

Israeli police on Saturday arrested a 25-year-old woman from Jerusalem on suspicion of pasting the posters on about 20 storefronts in Hebron. She also had thrown a rock through the windshield of an Arab car, police said.
Palestinians in Hebron were enraged when they discovered the posters of a pig donning an Arab headdress with the word Mohammed written on it in Arabic and English.
The drawing depicted the pig stomping with one foot on the Moslem holy book, the Koran, while holding a pen in the other. Islam and Judaism regard pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.
Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the poster.
"The only apology that we would accept is to withdraw the settlers from the heart of Hebron," said Rafiq al-Natsheh, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, during the demonstration.
Jewish settlers, who number about 400, remained in Hebron guarded by Israeli troops when Israel handed most of the city to Palestinian self-rule in January. More than 100,000 Arabs live in Hebron.
The city has been the scene of almost daily demonstrations along a confrontation line dividing Arab and Jewish areas in recent weeks.
Tensions have been fuelled by a freeze in Israeli-PLO peace talks over Israel's groundbreaking for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
